stimulus.text: A bus company in the hill town of Raniveri cut its fares by 20 per cent in January. Over the next three months, the number of daily passengers rose from 1,200 to 1,500. The company’s accountant noted that total daily fare income stayed at ₹30,000, because the extra passengers only just made up for the lower fare on each ticket. The town council also opened a new market near the bus station in February, which the accountant said might have drawn more shoppers onto the buses. The company has decided to keep the lower fares until June and then compare the figures again.
